arxiv-1912-08320.title: Garbage In, Garbage Out? Do Machine Learning Application Papers in Social Computing Report Where Human-Labeled Training Data Comes From? Conference: Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; January 27–30, 2020; Barcelona, Spain Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparenc
arxiv-1912-08320.creator: R. Stuart Geiger, Kevin Yu, Yanlai Yang, Mindy Dai, Jie Qiu, Rebekah Tang, Jenny Huang
arxiv-1912-08320.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by R. Stuart Geiger, Kevin Yu, Yanlai Yang, Mindy Dai, Jie Qiu, Rebekah Tang, Jenny Huang. Many machine learning projects for new application areas involve teams of humans who label data for a particular purpose, from hiring crowdworkers to the paper’s authors labeling the data themselves. Such a task is quite similar to (or a form of) structured content analysis, which is a longstanding methodology in the social sciences and humanities, with many established best practices.

arxiv-2101-09111.title: Uniquely orderable interval graphs Thanks: Both authors were partially supported by the Italian PRIN 2017 Grant “Mathematical Logic: models, sets, computability”.
arxiv-2101-09111.creator: Marta Fiori-Carones, Alberto Marcone
arxiv-2101-09111.description: Abstract . Interval graphs and interval orders are deeply linked. In fact, edges of an interval graphs represent the incomparability relation of an interval order, and in general, of different interval orders. The question about the conditions under which a given interval graph is associated to a unique interval order (up to duality) arises naturally.

arxiv-2110-12636.title: MOVER confidence intervals for a difference or ratio effect parameter under stratified sampling Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2110-12636.creator: Yongqiang Tang
arxiv-2110-12636.description: Abstract Stratification is commonly employed in clinical trials to reduce the chance covariate imbalances and increase the precision of the treatment effect estimate. We propose a general framework for constructing the confidence interval (CI) for a difference or ratio effect parameter under stratified sampling by the method of variance estimates recovery (MOVER).

arxiv-2211-13736.title: Black hole information recovery from gravitational waves
arxiv-2211-13736.creator: Louis Hamaide, Theo Torres
arxiv-2211-13736.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Louis Hamaide, Theo Torres. We study the classical and quantum black hole information in gravitational waves from a black hole’s history. We review the necessary concepts regarding quantum information in many-body systems to motivate information retrieval and content in gravitational waves. We then show the first step in an optimal information retrieval strategy is to search for information in gravitational waves, compared to searching for correlations in Hawking radiation.

arxiv-2301-05650.title: Contribution of Nuclear Excitation Electromagnetic Form Factors in C 12 {\rm{}^{12}C} and O 16 {\rm{}^{16}O} to the Coulomb Sum Rule
arxiv-2301-05650.creator: A. Bodek, M. E. Christy
arxiv-2301-05650.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A. Bodek, M. E. Christy. We report on empirical parameterizations of longitudinal and transverse nuclear excitation electromagnetic form factors in C 12 {\rm{}^{12}C} and O 16 {\rm{}^{16}O} . We extract the contribution of nuclear excitations to the Normalized Inelastic Coulomb Sum Rule ( S L ​ ( 𝐪 ) S_{L}({\bf q}) ) as a function of momentum transfer 𝐪 \bf q and find that it is significant (0.29 ± \pm 0.030 at 𝐪 \bf q = 0.22 GeV).

arxiv-2307-10452.title: Mass Loss in Evolved Stars
arxiv-2307-10452.creator: Lynn D. Matthews 1
arxiv-2307-10452.description: Abstract Intense mass loss through cool, low-velocity winds is a defining characteristic of low-to-intermediate mass stars during the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) evolutionary stage. Such winds return up ∼ \sim 80% of the initial stellar mass to the interstellar medium and play a major role in enriching it with dust and heavy elements.

arxiv-2310-15271.title: Elliptical micropillars for efficient generation and detection of coherent acoustic phonons
arxiv-2310-15271.creator: C. Xiang, A. Rodriguez, E. Cardozo de Oliveira, L. Le Gratiet, I. Sagnes, M. Morassi, A. Lemaître, N.D. Lanzillotti-Kimura
arxiv-2310-15271.description: Abstract ABSTRACT. Coherent acoustic phonon generation and detection assisted by optical resonances are at the core of efficient optophononic transduction processes. However, when dealing with a single optical resonance, the optimum generation and detection conditions take place at different laser wavelengths, i.e. different detunings from the cavity mode.

arxiv-2402-03784.title: AirPhyNet: Harnessing Physics-Guided Neural Networks for Air Quality Prediction
arxiv-2402-03784.creator: Kethmi Hirushini Hettige, Jiahao Ji, Shili Xiang, Cheng Long, Gao Cong, Jingyuan Wang
arxiv-2402-03784.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kethmi Hirushini Hettige, Jiahao Ji, Shili Xiang, Cheng Long, Gao Cong, Jingyuan Wang. Air quality prediction and modelling plays a pivotal role in public health and environment management, for individuals and authorities to make informed decisions. Although traditional data-driven models have shown promise in this domain, their long-term prediction accuracy can be limited, especially in scenarios with sparse or incomplete data and they often rely on black-box deep learning structures that lack solid physical foundation leading to reduced transparency and interpretability in predictions.

arxiv-2504-11469.title: Do Segmentation Models Understand Vascular Structure? A Blob-Based XAI Framework
arxiv-2504-11469.creator: Guillaume Garret, Antoine Vacavant, Carole Frindel
arxiv-2504-11469.description: Abstract 1 Abstract Deep learning models have achieved impressive performance in medical image segmentation, yet their black-box nature limits clinical adoption. In vascular applications, trustworthy segmentation should rely on both local image cues and global anatomical structures, such as vessel connectivity or branching. However, the extent to which models leverage such global context remains unclear.

arxiv-2602-04084.title: Uncertainty Principle for Vertex-Time Graph Signal Processing
arxiv-2602-04084.creator: Yanan Zhao, Xingchao Jian, Feng Ji, Wee Peng Tay, Antonio Ortega
arxiv-2602-04084.description: Abstract We present an uncertainty principle for graph signals in the vertex-time domain, unifying the classical time-frequency and graph uncertainty principles within a single framework. By defining vertex-time and spectral-frequency spreads, we quantify signal localization across these domains. Our framework identifies a class of signals that achieve maximum concentration in both the spatial and temporal domains.

arxiv-2602-22651.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Feedback
arxiv-2602-22651.creator: Ryotaro Honma, Tan Van Vu
arxiv-2602-22651.description: Abstract Fluctuations are intrinsic to microscopic systems and impose fundamental limits on nonequilibrium precision, as captured by the thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR), which links current fluctuations to entropy production. While feedback control is expected to further suppress fluctuations, its role within the TUR framework has remained unclear, particularly in quantum systems where control is inherently information-driven.

pmc-10545664.title: Immobilized enzyme microreactors for analysis of tryptic peptides in β-casein and β-lactoglobulin
pmc-10545664.creator: Agnieszka Rodzik, Viorica Railean, Paweł Pomastowski, Bogusław Buszewski, Michał Szumski
pmc-10545664.description: In this study, our primary objective was to develop an effective analytical method for studying trypsin-digested peptides of two proteins commonly found in cow's milk: β-casein (βCN) and β-lactoglobulin (βLG). To achieve this, we employed two distinct approaches: traditional in-gel protein digestion and protein digestion using immobilized enzyme microreactors (μ-IMER).

pmc-10575029.creator: Sisi Chang, Zhangzhao Weng, Chunmei Zhang, Shaohua Jiang, Gaigai Duan
pmc-10575029.description: Due to the rapid development of intelligent technology and the pursuit of green environmental protection, responsive materials with single response and actuation can no longer meet the requirements of modern technology for intelligence, diversification, and environmental friendliness. Therefore, intelligent responsive materials have received much attention.

pmc-11453294.title: 7481 Beyond the Operation Room: A Retrospective Study on Diabetes and Post-Operative Hyperglycemia Outcomes
pmc-11453294.creator: Polina Aron, Tasneem Zaihra Rizvi, Mary Beth Hodge, Karen St Jean, Jagriti Upadhyay
pmc-11453294.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11640425.title: Raman Spectroscopy Monitoring of Duck Egg Brining Process
pmc-11640425.creator: Huaizhou Jin, Yanxia Zou, Shangzhong Jin, Qiang Lin
pmc-11640425.description: Salted duck eggs are a popular food in China and a key ingredient in pastries such as mooncakes, valued for their unique flavors. In this study, we examined the influence of brining processes on duck eggs, focusing on salt concentration and the effect of added wine.

pmc-12799953.title: FAM117A and PIGU regulate the trilogy of gastric carcinogenesis
pmc-12799953.creator: Nianzhi Chen, Yueqiang Wen, Qingsong Liu, Jing Du, Dan Yao, Maoyuan Zhao, Cui Guo, Tingyao Wang, Jia Ma, Jianyuan Tang, Yumei Wang, Jinhao Zeng
pmc-12799953.description: Gastric cancer (GC) develops through a multistep process; however, the molecular mechanisms driving the progression from normal gastric mucosa to precancerous lesions and ultimately to GC remain incompletely understood. Here, this study performed whole-transcriptome sequencing and ATAC-seq on normal gastric mucosa (N), gastric precancerous lesions (P), and gastric tumor tissues (T) to profile chromatin accessibility, lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNAs.

pmc-13059232.title: Perception of e-professionalism of doctors of medicine and doctors of dental medicine among the general population in Croatia
pmc-13059232.creator: Marko Marelić, Joško Viskić, Kristijan Sedak, Marjeta Majer, Tea Vukušić Rukavina
pmc-13059232.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHealth care professionals’ (HCP) behaviour on social media (SM) can affect the perception that their colleagues, patients, and the general population have about them and their professionalism. There has been extensive research on the perception of HCPs’ e-professionalism within the student HCPs population and the practising HCPs, however, the research on perceptions of the general population has been missing so far.

pmc-13347292.title: Engineering Ga-containing dendritic MFI zeolites as safe-by-design hierarchical and immunomodulatory nanointerfaces
pmc-13347292.creator: Beatrice Fodor, Eva Romani, María del Mar Alonso-Doncel, Patricia Horcajada, David Serrano
pmc-13347292.description: The development of biocompatible and multifunctional inorganic nanomaterials is crucial in nanomedicine, requiring a balance of structural precision, safety, and therapeutic efficacy. In this work, we report the synthesis of nanometric dendritic gallium-containing MFI (d-Ga-MFI) zeolites from zeolite embryos functionalized with an amphiphilic organosilane, engineered as safe and bioactive inorganic interfaces.

pmc-13354630.title: Large fish eggs may lose their edge as temperature rises
pmc-13354630.creator: Francesca Leggieri, Oscar Nordahl, Markus Zöttl, Hanna Berggren, Petter Tibblin
pmc-13354630.description: It is a nearly universal truth that larger fish eggs have increased chances of survival. However, theory predicts that as temperatures rise, larger eggs may suffer the costs of oxygen limitation and lose their advantage altering the optimal life history trade-off between fecundity and offspring size.
